   117	# sanitize_to <src> <dest> <max-lines> — DESIGN.md invariant 6.  Build logs and
   118	# review findings never reach an agent unsanitized.  dispatch.sh sanitizes its
   119	# attachments again; this copy also covers the no-dispatcher fallback.
   120	sanitize_to() {
   121	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" <<'PY'
   122	import sys
   123	src, dest, max_lines = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
   124	try:
   125	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   126	except OSError:
   127	    raw = ""
   128	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
   129	keep = []
   130	for ch in raw:
   131	    o = ord(ch)
   132	    if ch in "\n\t" or (32 <= o < 127) or o > 159:
   133	        keep.append(ch)
   134	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")
   135	truncated = 0
   136	if len(lines) > max_lines:
   137	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   138	    lines = lines[-max_lines:]          # keep the tail: errors land last
   139	out = []
   140	if truncated:
   141	    out.append("... [%d earlier lines dropped by autofix.sh; full log on disk]"
   142	               % truncated)
   143	for line in lines:
   144	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   145	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   146	        line = " " + line
   147	    out.append(line)
   148	open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")
   149	PY
   150	}

   152	# acquire_fix_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   153	# Per-BRANCH lock WITH supersession: a newer invocation asks the running one to
   154	# stop at a phase boundary (the cancel-in-progress:true analogue of
   155	# auto-fix.yml:259-261).  Reviews use a per-PR lock without cancellation; the
   156	# split is deliberate (auto-fix.yml:29-32).
   157	acquire_fix_lock() {
   158	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   159	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   160	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   161	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   162	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   163	      warn "removing stale fix lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
   164	      rm -rf "$dir"
   165	      continue
   166	    fi
   167	    if [ "$waited" = 0 ]; then
   168	      log "a fix is already running for this branch (pid ${holder:-unknown}); requesting supersession"
   169	      printf 'superseded-by %s at %s\n' "$$" "$(now_utc)" >"$dir/cancel" 2>/dev/null || true
   170	    fi
   171	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   172	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the fix lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown}); it did not stop at a phase boundary"
   173	    fi
   174	    sleep 5
   175	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   176	  done
   177	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   178	  printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   179	  LOCK_HELD="$dir"
   180	}

   204	# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
   205	# registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.
   206	resolve_worktree() {
   207	  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   208	  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
   209	    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
   210	      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
   211	      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
   212	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
   213	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
   214	    return 0
   215	  fi
   216	  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   217	  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   218	  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
   219	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   220	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
   221	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   222	      return 0
   223	    fi
   224	    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
   225	  fi
   226	  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   227	  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
   228	    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"

   230	    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
   231	      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the fixer runs without a warmed build cache"
   232	  else
   233	    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the fix worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
   234	  fi
   235	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   236	}

    54	   status; `--adjudicated` needs an ADJUDICATION comment on the current head.

    99	## Naming and identity conventions

   108	  issue's.
   109	- **Fix commits**: subjects prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` / `[codex-review-fix]`

   112	  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`. Dispatched

   117	  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.
   118	
   119	## Telemetry (research-paper data)
   120	
   121	All appends are one-line JSON; schemas documented in `protocols/meta.md`.
   122	
   123	- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,
   124	  issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input, cached,
   125	  output, reasoning), exit status, dispatcher.
   126	- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` — one line per project stage/substage
   127	  transition with timestamps and manual token/agent tallies.
   128	- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` — one line per full build / cache event:
   129	  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.
   130	- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,
   131	  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
   132	- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an
   133	  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is
   134	  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.
   135	
   136	## Model policy
   137	
   138	- codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, ultra effort) drives orchestrator/prover/reviewer/
   139	  simplifier sessions (`codex exec`, `codex exec review`).
   140	- Claude-side subagents: easy/mechanical tasks run on Opus-tier; Fable-tier is
   141	  reserved for hard reasoning (proof strategy, protocol synthesis, adversarial
   142	  verification).
   143	- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never
   144	  reviews its own diff.
   270	  repository learned this the expensive way: a workflow-level concurrency
   271	  group let an unrelated event cancel an in-progress fix, and the fix was to
   272	  scope the group correctly rather than to widen it (`auto-fix.yml:29-32`).
   273	- The build lock is a separate mechanism: one full `lake build` machine-wide
   274	  at a time (`DESIGN.md` invariant 7, `build-cache.md`). A dispatched session
   275	  inherits that discipline; it does not get its own exemption.
   276	
   277	## 9. Kill switches
   278	
   279	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable their subsystem
   280	**only** when set to the literal string `false`. Unset, empty, `0`, `no` and
   281	`False` all mean enabled (`DESIGN.md` invariant 4 — the parent's repo
   282	variables had exactly this semantics, and reading unset as disabled would
   283	silently stop the whole review layer).
   284	
   285	`dispatch.sh` enforces `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for the `reviewer` role and
   286	exits 3, including for the forced end-of-cap review: a disabled review layer

   288	fix sessions; no role name identifies one, so `dispatch.sh` cannot.
   289	
   290	## 10. What a session leaves behind
   291	
   292	| Artifact | Path | Lifetime |
   293	|---|---|---|
   294	| event stream | `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` | permanent, committed — this is the archive |
   295	| final message | `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.last.md` | permanent, committed |
   296	| registry line | `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` | permanent, append-only |
   297	| codex rollout | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*-<thread-id>.jsonl` | outside the repo; path recorded, contents not relied on |
   298	| worktree | `.worktrees/<branch>` | removed at archival |
   299	| locks | `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` | released at exit |
   300	
   301	The registry line schema is in `meta.md`. Beyond it, `dispatch.sh` records
   302	`turns` (completed model turns), `capture` (repo-relative path to the event
   303	stream) and, when resolvable, `rollout`. Token usage is summed over
   304	`turn.completed` events and normalized to
   305	`{input, cached_input, cache_write, output, reasoning}`; `dispatch.sh` writes
   306	`status: done` or `failed` at the end of a run, and `active` is reserved for
   307	backfilled or externally started sessions.

   309	## 11. Exit codes
   310	
   311	`dispatch.sh` distinguishes its own refusals from the agent's outcome:
   312	
   313	| Code | Meaning |
   314	|---|---|
   315	| 0 | session ran and codex exited 0 |

   104	class FakeGitHub:
   105	    """A fake ``gh`` binary plus its route table, all inside one tempdir."""
   106	
   107	    def __init__(self, tmp: Path) -> None:
   108	        self.tmp = tmp
   109	        self.binary = tmp / "gh"
   110	        self.binary.write_text(FAKE_GH, encoding="utf-8")
   111	        self.binary.chmod(0o755)
   112	        self.spool = tmp / "gh-calls.jsonl"
   113	        self.routes_path = tmp / "gh-routes.json"
   114	        self.routes: list[dict] = []
   115	        self._flush()
   116	
   117	    def route(self, path: str, body=None, *, method: str = "GET",
   118	              fail: bool = False, once: bool = False) -> "FakeGitHub":
   119	        """Declare one reply.  *path* is a regex against the repo-relative route.
   120	
   121	        Rules match in declaration order, so a ``once=True`` rule in front of a
   122	        broader one models "state changed between two reads" — exactly the
   123	        adoption paths at ``gh_common.py:216-224`` and ``:336-343``.
   124	        """
   125	        rule: dict = {"path": path, "method": method}
   126	        if body is not None:
   127	            rule["body"] = body
   128	        if fail:
   129	            rule["fail"] = True
   130	        if once:
   131	            rule["once"] = True
   132	        self.routes.append(rule)
   133	        self._flush()
   134	        return self
   135	
   136	    def reset(self) -> None:
   137	        """Forget the routes and the call log; used between gate scenarios."""
   138	        self.routes = []
   139	        self._flush()
   140	        for path in (self.spool, Path(str(self.spool) + ".state")):
   141	            if path.exists():
   142	                path.unlink()
   143	
   144	    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
   145	        return {"MIPSTARRE_GH": str(self.binary),
   146	                "MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO": REPO,
   147	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_SPOOL": str(self.spool),
   148	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_ROUTES": str(self.routes_path)}
   149	
   150	    def calls(self) -> list[dict]:
   151	        if not self.spool.exists():
   152	            return []
   153	        return [json.loads(line) for line in
   154	                self.spool.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line]
   155	
   156	    def payloads(self, method: str, pattern: str) -> list[dict]:
   157	        """Decoded request bodies of the calls matching *method* and *pattern*."""
   158	        return [json.loads(call["stdin"]) for call in self.calls()
   159	                if call["method"] == method and re.search(pattern, call["rel"])
   160	                and call["stdin"]]
   161	
   162	    def _flush(self) -> None:
   163	        self.routes_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.routes), encoding="utf-8")

   411	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   412	# Repository hygiene — the retired trees stay retired
   413	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
   414	
   415	#: A path segment into the archived registries.  The REST API also speaks
   416	#: ``issues/...``, so the two are told apart by what follows: a route always
   417	#: continues with an f-string field (``issues/{number}/comments``) or with
   418	#: ``comments/{id}`` (gh_common.py:213), while a tree reference continues with a
   419	#: literal id, glob or filename.
   420	_TREE_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.-])(?:issues|prs)/")
   421	_REST_ROUTE_RE = re.compile(r"^issues/(?:\{|comments/\{)")
   422	
   423	#: The other shape a tree reference takes: a join onto the repository root.
   424	_TREE_JOIN_RE = re.compile(
   425	    r"""(?:\$\{?ROOT\}?|\$\{?REPO_ROOT\}?|repo_root|REPO_ROOT)\s*/\s*["']?(?:issues|prs)\b""")
   426

   428	def _active_source(path: Path) -> str:
   429	    """The file's live code: comments and docstrings blanked, line numbers kept.
   430	
   431	    Every surviving mention of the registries is historical narration ("Pre-0007
   432	    this wrote ``prs/<id>-<slug>/pr.md``", issue_new.py:2-5), so a grep over raw
   433	    text cannot express the rule.  Python comments come from ``tokenize`` (a
   434	    ``#`` inside a string is not a comment token) and docstrings from ``ast``;
   435	    shell keeps only its non-comment lines.
   436	    """
   437	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   438	    if path.suffix == ".sh":
   439	        return "\n".join("" if line.lstrip().startswith("#") else line
   440	                         for line in text.splitlines())
   441	    lines = text.splitlines()
   442	    docstring_lines: set[int] = set()
   443	    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(text)):
   444	        if isinstance(node, (ast.Module, ast.ClassDef, ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   445	            if ast.get_docstring(node, clean=False) is not None:
   446	                first = node.body[0]
   447	                docstring_lines.update(range(first.lineno, (first.end_lineno or first.lineno) + 1))
   448	    for token in tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(text).readline):
   449	        if token.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
   450	            row, column = token.start
   451	            lines[row - 1] = lines[row - 1][:column]
   452	    return "\n".join("" if number + 1 in docstring_lines else line
   453	                     for number, line in enumerate(lines))
   454

   456	class RegistryHygieneTests(unittest.TestCase):
   457	    def test_no_live_tool_reaches_for_the_retired_issue_or_pr_trees(self) -> None:
   458	        """The registries are archived read-only; nothing in ``local/bin`` reads them.
   459	
   460	        A single surviving path join is enough to reintroduce the split brain
   461	        issue 0007 removed — a tool that consults a stale local record instead of
   462	        GitHub fails open rather than closed.
   463	        """
   464	        offenders: list[str] = []
   465	        tools = sorted(p for p in LOCAL_BIN.iterdir() if p.suffix in (".py", ".sh"))
   466	        self.assertGreater(len(tools), 10, "the local/bin tool set did not load")
   467	        for tool in tools:
   468	            source = _active_source(tool)
   469	            for number, line in enumerate(source.splitlines(), start=1):
   470	                for hit in _TREE_PATH_RE.finditer(line):
   471	                    if not _REST_ROUTE_RE.match(line[hit.start():]):
   472	                        offenders.append(f"{tool.name}:{number}: {line.strip()}")
   473	                if _TREE_JOIN_RE.search(line):
   474	                    offenders.append(f"{tool.name}:{number}: {line.strip()}")
   475	        self.assertEqual(offenders, [], "live registry-tree references:\n" + "\n".join(offenders))

     5	
     6	## Standing principles

    15	   a telemetry observation (e.g. repeated duplicate builds in
    16	   `builds.jsonl`), or an upstream policy decision by the user. No trigger,
    17	   no amendment.
    18	3. **The parent repo is precedent, not law.** The GitHub-era mechanism (frozen
    19	   under `.github/`, mapped in `local/DESIGN.md`) is the default answer to
    20	   "how should this work?"; deviations are fine when the local setting
    21	   genuinely differs, and must be recorded in `EVOLUTION.md` with the reason.

    25	   notices when resources were exhausted. Prefer the cheapest mechanism that

    16	
    17	The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull

    20	invocation, one manifest, one exit code.
    21	
    22	```

    24	                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]

    27	`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the

    30	runs everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary
    31	checkout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the
    32	run starts.

    34	Exit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at
    35	least one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start

   145	
   146	The count is derived from the branch's own history, not from a stored field:

+## 2026-09-01 — GitHub becomes the workflow authority (lean port)
+
+**Trigger:** owner decision 2026-08-31 (follow-on to the re-hybridization
+entry); executed 2026-09-01 after the scope reset recorded below.
+
+**Change:** The local issue tree and PR registry are retired.  GitHub
+(`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`) is the single source of truth for issues (native
+sub-issues replace `parent`/`children` frontmatter), PRs, CI evidence
+(per-step commit statuses `local-ci/<step>` plus `local-ci/summary` and
+`local-review/summary` on the exact head SHA), review verdicts (COMMENT
+reviews bound to a commit id — a single-account repo cannot self-APPROVE, so
+adverseness travels in the failing `local-review/summary` status), and merges
+(REST merge guarded by the exact-SHA `sha` parameter, verified by merge-commit
+topology).  All GitHub traffic goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py`; shared
+non-registry helpers moved to `local/bin/wf_util.py`.  `track.py`,
+`validate_tree.py`, `export_issues.py`, and `local/labels.yml` are deleted —
+GitHub provides what they reimplemented.  The registries were archived
+verbatim first (`results/telemetry/registry-archive/`, commit c8f1999) and
+stay read-only research data; `github-sync.sh` now also writes a read-only
+JSON snapshot of open issues/PRs under `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`
+for offline forensics — never lifecycle input.

+**Expected effect:** CI and reviews still execute locally on this machine;
+GitHub stores the evidence.
+
+## 2026-09-01 — Scope control for workflow changes (incident amendment)
+
+**Trigger:** events.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild.  The first
+implementation of the entry above grew, in ~17 hours and 21 commits, into a
++14.6k-line unreviewed rewrite of the whole layer — a 2,761-line bespoke
+GitHub API client, a 643-line lock manager, a 5,649-line test suite wired
+into the commit and push hooks (≈10 minutes per commit), an actor-verification
+regime and a branch-protection evaluator nobody asked for — while the actual
+product (the Lean formalization; PR #5's 17 findings) sat untouched.  The
+owner paused the session, archived the branch as research data
+(`telemetry/issue-0007-overbuilt`), and rebuilt the port lean.
+
+**Change:** amendment (now also in `local/personas/main.md`):
+
+1. The product is the Lean formalization.  `local/` is scaffolding; scaffolding
+   work is a cost center, budgeted by default at ≤2 hours wall time and ≤400
+   changed lines per episode.  Hitting the budget means stop, commit what
+   stands, record the state, and escalate to the owner — not push through.
+2. Git hooks must finish in under 60 seconds on a typical commit; heavier
+   verification belongs to CI steps.
+3. No new abstraction layers (API clients, lock managers, frameworks) and no
+   rewrites of working, reviewed code without an explicit owner directive;
+   prefer the smallest diff that satisfies the brief, and prefer `gh` + the
+   REST API over reimplementation.
+4. After any workflow change merges, the next dispatched work item MUST be a
+   mathematics item.  Two consecutive workflow-only episodes require owner
+   approval.
+
+**Expected effect:** scaffolding episodes stay bounded and auditable, and the
+work item after a merged workflow change is mathematics.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `local/bin/ci.sh:683` — `--base` loses its partial-run flag and can publish green evidence for an empty diff
- [ ] F2 (blocker) `local/bin/pr_merge.py:283` — The merge gate ignores the current base SHA and can merge an untested base/head combination
- [ ] F3 (blocker) `local/bin/autofix.sh:410` — An unresolved base resets the fix counter and disables the iteration cap
- [ ] F4 (changes) `local/bin/review.sh:1016` — Review writes tracked telemetry into the primary checkout that the merge gate requires clean
- [ ] F5 (changes) `local/personas/prover.md:23` — Active personas still direct agents to the deleted local issue registry
- [ ] F6 (changes) `local/protocols/ci.md:110` — The normative workflow-gating contract no longer matches `ci.sh`
- [ ] F7 (changes) `local/protocols/ci.md:131` — Documented manifest paths and partial-run modes disagree with the implementation
- [ ] F8 (changes) `.githooks/pre-commit:31` — Deletion-only workflow commits bypass the new infrastructure-size guard

## Review

**F1.** Line 535 sets `PARTIAL=1` for `--base`, but line 683 unconditionally restores `PARTIAL=0`. Pointing the base at the PR head therefore produces no changed files, records every gate as skipped-success, and publishes canonical statuses. The round-two repair remains ineffective. Preserve the existing flag and add an entrypoint test proving that `--base` performs no GitHub mutations.

**F2.** `run_gate` retains only `base.ref`; CI and review evidence are bound solely to the feature head. The merge request sends only `{"sha": head}`, and `gh_common.merge_pr` accepts any first parent. The exact-head manifest used merge base `178d781`, while the supplied branch merge base is `d612c96` and current `main`/`github/main` is `30932ab`; the reviewed head is not based on that current tip. Bind evidence to `base.sha`, require an up-to-date branch, or test and identify a synthetic merge result.

**F3.** A failed `merge-base "$BASE" "$LOCAL_TIP"` emits a warning, sets `FIX_ITERATIONS=0`, and proceeds. Repeated invocations can consequently create unlimited fixer commits. Resolve the same remote/local base candidates used by the merge gate and fail closed when none resolves.

**F4.** `results/telemetry/reviews/` is tracked, so the copy makes the primary checkout dirty after review; `pr_merge.py:121-124` then refuses it. Committing that ledger directly to `main` instead advances the base and exposes F2, while also conflicting with `issues-prs.md`’s exclusive merge path. Keep this artifact in runtime storage or define a convergent archival phase outside the pre-merge gate.

**F5.** The previous persona repair updated orchestrator/scout only. `prover.md:23` and `splitter.md:26` still require issue files, while `blueprint.md:67-69` denies the GitHub issue tracker and prescribes `issues/...` comments. These sessions must consume the GitHub issue through the dispatcher’s untrusted context.

**F6-F7.** The protocol says the workflow area contains three files, but `ci.sh:643-644` now includes all `local/bin/*`, `local/protocols/*`, and `.githooks/*`. It also documents `$CACHE_ROOT/ci/<pr>/<sha>` while code writes `$CACHE_ROOT/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<sha>`, and omits `--base` from partial modes. Synchronize the normative protocol and add the amendment record required by `meta.md`.

**F8.** The initial staged-file query excludes `D` and exits before the scope guard. A deletion-only change can therefore remove more than 400 workflow lines without evaluation. Include deletions in the initial filter or run the guard before that early exit.

The exact-head CI manifest reports success and 430 tests passed; shell syntax and `git diff --check` also pass. The nine new workflow tests do not invoke `ci.sh`, `review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, or an actual merge, which leaves the critical entrypoint behavior above uncovered. No Lean, blueprint, or paper-gap declarations changed, so source-statement fidelity is not implicated.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
